metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive extraction from 1880 Colonial Office List covering all 37 British colonies and territories. Detailed data extracted from 23 colonies (Caribbean: Bahamas, Bermudas, Jamaica, Trinidad; South America: British Guiana; North America: Newfoundland; Africa: Cape of Good Hope, Natal, Gold Coast, St. Helena, Mauritius; Asia: Ceylon, Hong Kong, Straits Settlements, Labuan; Pacific: Fiji, Falkland Islands; Europe/Mediterranean: Heligoland, Gibraltar, Malta; Australia: New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland). Summary data included for remaining 14 colonies. Data includes geographic entities, government officials with complete salary details, institutions, economic statistics (revenue/expenditure/trade), infrastructure (railways, telegraphs, postal), demographics with population breakdowns, and historical events. All toponyms preserved with original historical spelling. Financial data in original currencies (£, Rs., $). This extraction focuses on explicitly stated information only, with no synthesis or modernization.

places.name: Heligoland
places.description: An island situated in the North Sea, opposite, and about 25 miles from, the mouth of the Elbe. Area, inclusive of the adjacent island termed 'Sandy,' three-quarters of a square mile.

places.name: Gibraltar
places.description: The Rock of Gibraltar. An elevated promontory, running southwards. Its greatest elevation is 1,439 feet, its length is 2½ miles, and its greatest breadth ¾ of a mile.

places.name: Bahamas
places.description: A chain of islands. The group is composed of about 20 inhabited islands and an immense number of islets and rocks.

places.name: Nassau
places.description: The capital, located on New Providence island

places.name: New Providence
places.description: Principal island containing the capital, Nassau

places.name: Jamaica
places.description: An island situated in the Caribbean Sea, and to the southward of the eastern extremity of the Island of Cuba. It is the largest of the British West Indies, being 140 miles in length, and 50 in extreme breadth.

places.name: Bermudas
places.description: Or Somers' Islands, a cluster of about 100 small islands, situated on the western side of the Atlantic Ocean, at a distance of about 580 miles from the nearest land, viz. Cape Hatteras in North Carolina.

places.name: British Guiana
places.description: A portion of the South American Continent, extending from east to west about 200 miles. It includes the settlements of Demerara, Essequebo, and Berbice. Bounded on the east by Dutch Guiana (River Corentyn), on the south by Brazil, on the west by Venezuela, and on the north by the Atlantic Ocean.

places.name: Ceylon
places.description: An island situated in the Indian Ocean, off the southern extremity of Hindostan. Extreme length from Point Palmyra to Dondera Head is 266 miles; greatest width 140½ miles.

places.name: Fiji Islands
places.description: About 255 islands, of which 80 are inhabited. The larger islands are mostly mountainous, rising abruptly from the shores to an altitude of from 2,000 to 6,000 feet.

places.name: Falkland Islands
places.description: Situated in the South Atlantic Ocean. Consist of the East Falkland (area 3,000 square miles), the West Falkland (2,300 square miles), and about 100 small islands with an area of nearly 1,200 square miles.

places.name: Hong Kong
places.description: One of a number of islands situated off the south-eastern coast of China, at the mouth of the Canton River. About 40 miles east of Macao. The island is an irregular ridge, its length is about 11 miles, its breadth from 2 to 5 miles.

places.name: Labuan
places.description: Situated on the north-west coast of Borneo, distant from the coast at the nearest point about six miles, and from Brunei about thirty miles.

places.name: Malta
places.description: Islands of Malta, Gozo, and Comino. Malta is highly cultivated; its principal products are cotton and corn.

places.name: Mauritius
places.description: An island lying in the Indian Ocean. Greatest length from Cape Malheureux to Point Desnus is 39 miles, and its widest part 34 miles across. Divided into nine districts.

places.name: St. Helena
places.description: An island in the South Atlantic Ocean, 800 miles S.E. of Ascension, and 1,200 miles from the coast of South Africa. 10½ miles long and 6½ broad.

places.name: Cape of Good Hope
places.description: The Cape Colony, with adjacent territories (Basutoland and British Transkei), contains an area of 222,308 square miles; the area of the Colony being 199,950, of Basutoland 10,293, and of the Transkeian territories 12,065 square miles. Bounded on the north by the Orange River, on the north-east by Natal, and on the east by certain districts of Native Kaffraria.

places.name: Cape Town
places.description: The capital. Has a population of 33,239, and with suburbs, 45,240. Laid out at right angles, and contains numerous handsome shops, offices, and churches.

places.name: Newfoundland
places.description: Island situated between 46° 30' and 51° 39' N. lat., and 52° 15' and 59° 60' W. long., on the north-east side of the Gulf of St. Lawrence. Greatest length from north to south is 350 miles, and average breadth about 130.

places.name: Natal
places.description: Colony derives its name from fact of its discovery by Vasco de Gama on Christmas-day, 1497. Lies on the south-east coast of Africa, about eight hundred miles from the Cape of Good Hope. Bounded by the Tugela and Umzimkulu Rivers, and by the Drakensberg Mountains. Has a seaboard of one hundred and seventy miles.

places.name: Pietermaritzburg
places.description: Capital of Natal

places.name: Trinidad
places.description: Island lies to the eastward of Venezuela. Separated from the continent of America by the Gulf of Paria. First discovered by Columbus on his third voyage, on the 31st July, 1496.

places.name: Port of Spain
places.description: Chief town and principal port, population 30,000. Situated on a gently inclined plain, near the north-east angle of the Gulf of Paria.

places.name: New South Wales
places.description: Colony situated on the eastern coast of the Australian continent. First settlement was formed in 1788. Contains 119,000,000 acres, of which 613,642 acres are under crop.

places.name: Sydney
places.description: Seat of Government

places.name: Victoria
places.description: Most populous and wealthy of the Australasian colonies. Situated at the south-east of the Continent of Australia. Extreme length from east to west is about 420 geographical miles, greatest breadth about 250. Separated from New South Wales in 1851.

places.name: Melbourne
places.description: Capital of Victoria. Most populous city in Australasia, having (in 1879), with its suburbs, a population of 256,477. First settlers established themselves so recently as in 1835.

places.name: Queensland
places.description: Whole colony comprises 669,520 square miles, or 428,492,800 acres. Southern boundary line formed by 29th parallel of south latitude. Eastern seaboard extends about 1,500 miles from Point Danger to Cape York.

places.name: Brisbane
places.description: Capital of the Colony. Population of 24,603 resident within municipal limits, and 32,012 within the census district. Mean external shade temperature 70°.

places.name: Straits Settlements
places.description: Comprise Singapore, Penang, and Malacca. Transferred from control of Indian Government to Secretary of State for Colonies on 1st April, 1867.

places.name: Singapore
places.description: Island about 27 miles long by 14 wide, situated at southern extremity of Malayan Peninsula. Seat of Government is the town of Singapore, at the southern point of the island.

places.name: The Gold Coast Colony
places.description: Comprises British Settlements on the Gold Coast and at Lagos. Constituted by Charter bearing date 24th July 1874. Name generally given to portion of Upper Guinea between 5° W. long. and 2° E. long. Includes settlements of Axim, Dixcove, Sekondie, Elmina, Cape Coast Castle, Anamaboe, Accra, and Addah.

infrastructure.name: Kingston to Old Harbour Railway
infrastructure.notes: Since the purchase of the line by the Government, an extension to Portus and Linstead is in contemplation

infrastructure.name: Jamaica Telegraph
infrastructure.notes: Telegraphic communication with Europe is complete. Jamaica is the first British possession in the West Indies which the cable touches at, whence it branches away via St. Thomas, Barbados, &c., to Demerara, and in the opposite direction to the Isthmus of Panama.

infrastructure.name: Ceylon Telegraph
infrastructure.notes: The principal towns are connected by the telegraph, which is worked in connection with the Indian telegraph system

infrastructure.name: Cape Colony Railways
infrastructure.notes: Divided into three groups: Western System 401½ miles; Midland and North-eastern System 401½ miles; Border System 167½ miles. Gauge of 3 ft. 6 in. Total appropriations 8,277,720£, spent up to 31st December 1878: 6,925,464£

infrastructure.name: St. George's Causeway
infrastructure.notes: Island of St. George's was connected with the main island by a causeway and road, commenced in 1866, and completed in 1871. An iron girder swing-bridge still permits the passage of vessels.

infrastructure.name: Pietermaritzburg to Durban Railway
infrastructure.notes: First sod turned 1st January 1876. Nearly completed in 1880. Branch to Verulam 19½ miles, branch to Isipingo River 7 miles.

infrastructure.name: Port of Spain to Arima Railway
infrastructure.notes: Opened in 1876. Couva line (24 miles from Port of Spain) to be in full work in 1880. Extension to San Fernando (7 miles) commenced.

infrastructure.name: Victorian Railways
infrastructure.notes: 1,502 miles completed and in full operation. 72 miles in course of construction.
